brief.title: Your trip at a glance
brief.text:
A private expedition on the Sea of Cortez, built around the wind. Kite is the center of the trip: the best wind windows come first, and sailing, swimming, meals and rest fit around them.

While she rides with Lou, he can head out on his wing. Eagle Ray Expeditions brings the boat, the crew, the kitchen and the logistics, so the only thing you plan is when to get in the water.

Captain, chef and Lou as Expedition Leader

Airport pickup and private transfer included

about.title: Meet Lou
about.quote: The calmness of the deep and the glassy water.
about.text:
I've spent 15 years on sailboats around the world: the Bahamas, Polynesia, Brittany, the Caribbean and the Sea of Cortez. I've skippered boats from a Lagoon 41 to a Lagoon 62, and I'm a certified marine engineer, so I know the boat from the helm to the engine room.

I'm an IKO-certified kite instructor, and I also teach sailing and freediving. On this trip I'm your Expedition Leader and, for her, the coach she already knows from her lessons. While she rides with me, he can head out on his wing.

Years of all of it in Baja have taught me to read the wind and the people on the water, and to adjust the day as it goes. What I look for in guests is the spark in their eyes when the sea starts to work on them.

trips.title: Two ways to do it

items.name: 3 nights / 4 days
items.text: A short private escape around the wind: four days on the water, with kite sessions whenever the wind allows.

items.name: 5 nights / 6 days
items.text: More days to wait for the best wind and use it. It also leaves room for a longer day out toward Isla Cerralvo, if conditions and Lou say yes.

trips.note: Want more or fewer nights? Ask us.

boats.title: The boat
boats.pricingText: Prices are for the whole boat and the two of you, in US dollars. They are valid for the kite season, December to April. Christmas, New Year and Holy Week dates on request.

options.name: Lagoon 450F
options.intro:
A 45-foot catamaran with four double cabins and four bathrooms, built in 2018 and refitted in 2024.

Why a catamaran works for kite: a wide deck to rig on, a stable boat at anchor, and the option to anchor close to shore. The flybridge, the inflatable dock and the tender make getting in and out of the water easy.

This boat or a similar one, subject to availability for your dates.
features: Air conditioning in every cabin and in the saloon

The cockpit table seats ten, so lunch at anchor happens outside, and the swim platform lowers to the waterline. Below deck: three suites and three bathrooms.

kite.title: Kite and wing
kite.text:
Kite gear for her is included. He brings his own wing setup, and it is welcome on board.

Depending on the day, you launch from the boat or from the beach, always depending on the wind.
items: Her gear: kite, board, harness, wetsuit, helmet or impact vest [list to confirm with Lou]
His gear: bring your own wing setup, welcome on board
Launch: from the boat or the beach, depending on the day
On the water: tender support [to confirm with Lou]
Spots: Espíritu Santo and La Ventana, depending on the wind

days.title: The wind decides
days.text:
Each day, the captain and Lou choose where to anchor and where to ride, based on the wind and the sea state. Around La Ventana the wind tends to fill in during the afternoon, so the day follows it.

### When the wind is up
The tender goes to the water, she rides with Lou, and he heads out on his wing.

### When it isn't
Snorkel, paddleboard and kayak off the boat, a long lunch at anchor, or a sail to the next anchorage.

### On the 5-night trip
If conditions and Lou say yes, there may be a longer day out toward Isla Cerralvo. It is a possibility, not a fixed activity.
days.note: The final plan is set by the captain and Lou, according to wind and sea conditions.

food.text: Three meals a day, cooked on board by your chef: breakfast, lunch and dinner. Meals fit around the wind, so lunch can wait if the best wind is at noon.

meals.text: Fresh fruit and something hot, before the day starts.

meals.name: Lunch

meals.name: Dinner

crew.title: Your crew
crew.text:
Every expedition has a crew of three: a captain who knows these waters well, a chef who cooks with local produce and what the sea gives that week, and an Expedition Leader who looks after the group.

We choose them for their love of the sea and for how they share it with other people. They come from sailing, diving and hospitality (Ritz-Carlton, Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental).
crew.explainText:
An Expedition Leader is not a guide who follows a script, and not a host who serves the table. It is the Eagle Ray Expeditions person who stays with you the whole trip and answers for how it goes.

They know the group, decide with the captain when to swim and when to sail, look after everyone in the water, and take care of the details so you don't have to think about them.

That is the difference from chartering a boat with a crew: here someone is in charge of your experience, not only of the navigation. On this trip, that person is also her kite coach.

leader.imageAlt: Lou, Expedition Leader and kite instructor
leader.name: Lou
leader.role: Your Expedition Leader and her kite coach
leader.text:
Lou is the person in charge of making the trip work for you: the wind, the anchorages, the water and the day.

Lou also coaches her on the kite, as in her lessons, and keeps an eye on the water while the two of you ride.

season.title: The wind in season
season.text:
The season runs from November to March. The wind comes from the north and northwest, and around La Ventana it tends to fill in during the afternoon.
